feed.title: antxiko — commented disassemblies of 8-bit games
feed.subtitle: Old 8-bit binaries taken apart byte by byte and commented, with the tools to rebuild them: nothing gets claimed that the binary does not show, and the source has to give the original back, byte for byte. Right now that means 70 MSX games.

entry.title: Dunk Shot: the MSX2 patch now also fits the corrected ROM
entry.summary: There is a second Dunk Shot ROM (GoodMSX [a]) that fixes bugs in the fouls and the scoring. It is the same program rebuilt, with almost everything at other addresses, so the old IPS cannot be used on it: it has its own, and the same tool builds both. On an NMS 8250 it goes from 72.5 to 1.4 sprites not drawn per frame; on an MSX it plays as the original. Its commented disassembly and what differs between the two ROMs are in the Dunk Shot disassembly repository.

entry.title: King's Valley II: the MSX2 sprites drawn as the V9938 draws them
entry.summary: On the MSX2, Vick and the enemies are pairs of sprites whose colours are ORed together where they overlap; the second sprite was being left out wherever it did not overlap the first, so Vick's face came out black. Now Vick, the enemies, the demos and the sequences match openMSX. Also: the MSX objects sheet on a black background, and the SECRET COMMAND hints, F??T???L and ??Y?????, are FESTIVAL and TRYAGAIN: they only show with the Game Master 2 plugged in.

entry.title: King's Valley II: the MSX and MSX2 cartridges, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1988 King's Valley II, The Seal of El Giza, on its two cartridges (RC-760 for MSX, RC-761 for MSX2) in a single listing: both 100% explained and commented to 40%. The six pyramids with their 60 stages and 154 screens, Vick with each of his six tools, the four enemies with their names from the editor, the demos, the editor and where it saves, the passwords FESTIVAL and TRYAGAIN, the two hidden minigames and 16 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine; everything drawn by running the cartridge and checked against openMSX.

entry.title: Parodius: Tako saves the Earth, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1988 Parodius for MSX, 100% explained and commented to 40.1%. The six stages and the three secret ones with their whole maps, the five characters with every weapon firing, the six bosses, the explosions that shout in kana, the words you can type in the pause, the game saved on the Game Master 2, the intro and the ending translated, and 18 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine; everything checked against openMSX.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: enemies named after metal bands
entry.summary: In the MSX version the enemies carry heavy metal band names: Celtic Frost, Nuclear Assault, M.O.D., Leper Messiah, Led Zep, Ozzy, Exodus... The enemies page now lists all 43, each with the series enemy it matches.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: the bosses get their names
entry.summary: The cartridge does not name its bosses, but the MSX version has its own: Golem, Cruiser Tetran, Center Core, Dead End, Seducer, Enigma, Outer Limits and Metal Slave. Each one is matched to its boss by the stage, taken from the ROM's cards, and by its look.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: every route, enemy and boss on its page
entry.summary: The stages page now shows the seven whole routes one after another, the enemies page the sheet of each stage, and the bosses page the eight bosses and the stage 7 core, each with its title.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: the web in three blocks
entry.summary: The pages are rearranged: first the game (the stages, the ship and its weapons, the enemies, the bosses, the sequences, the music and the texts), then the curiosities, and at the end what is under the hood. The home page keeps the numbers and the list of pages. The old addresses lead to the new pages.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: the intro, the story and every weapon, animated
entry.summary: The intro, the whole story and the take-off as animations, every frame painted from openMSX's VRAM the way the TMS9918 paints it. The seven gauge boxes with the names of their weapons taken from the ROM, and the ship firing each one: NORMAL, TWIN, TRIPLE, the missiles, RIPPLE, ARMING, LASER, METEO, SCREW, the options, the F.FIELD and the bombs. Plus the capsules and the six items enemies drop. The bosses have no names in the cartridge, in English or Japanese. And the Konami screen gets its blue background back.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: the game page, tidied up
entry.summary: One picture per section with its caption, and the rest in tables of links: the seven routes, the enemies of each stage and the bosses. The intro and both endings are in now, screen by screen, each one identical pixel for pixel to openMSX's VRAM.

entry.title: Salamander - Operation X: Konami's MSX shooter, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1987 Salamander for MSX, 100% explained and commented to 44.6%. The seven stages with their whole routes (in three of them the screen turns through another map), the planet choice for stages 3 to 5, the eight bosses, both endings, and stage 7, OPERATION X, which only exists with Nemesis 2 in the other slot and takes its graphics from it. 20 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine; everything checked against openMSX.

entry.title: The Pro Yakyuu Gekitotsu Pennant Race: the finished-game sheet
entry.summary: The last screen: each team's at-bats, hits, home runs, strikeouts and walks, from a CPU against CPU game played to the end in openMSX at full speed, and checked at 0 bytes different. Its scrambled top band is explained too: the game clears the screen in four rectangles and leaves that band with whatever was there.

entry.title: The Pro Yakyuu Gekitotsu Pennant Race: MEMBER CHANGE and the bases windows
entry.summary: Two more screens drawn from the code and checked byte for byte against openMSX: the substitution screen, reached from the pause, and the two little windows with first and third base on the pitching screen.

entry.title: The Pro Yakyuu Gekitotsu Pennant Race: the whole field and every sign, checked
entry.summary: The left and right field zones, which the demo never shows, are now checked against the openMSX VRAM from a WATCH game: 256 of 256 lines and 248 of 256, the other 8 being the OUT the game writes on top. The six pitching signs are checked too, LUCKY 7 by putting the seventh inning in RAM before the first pitch.

entry.title: The Pro Yakyuu Gekitotsu Pennant Race: the menus
entry.summary: Seven more screens drawn from the code: choosing the teams, the starting pitchers, STARTING LINE-UP, TEAM EDIT, LEAGUE SELECTION, the PENNANT round and the results and standings, with its four-step long division for the percentage. Each one checked against the openMSX VRAM at 0 bytes different. Also: the pitching screen now matches in 818 of 864 blocks, after fixing how a VDP LINE is drawn.

entry.title: The Pro Yakyuu Gekitotsu Pennant Race: the players, animated
entry.summary: The batter's swing, the pitcher's four styles and the fielders and runners on the field, as GIFs built the way the game builds them: sprite attributes, colour indices and the patterns it copies piece by piece from the VRAM, with the timing of its code. Also the Konami logo, the animated intro, the mode menu and the pitching signs. Checked byte for byte against the openMSX VRAM.

entry.title: The Pro Yakyuu Gekitotsu Pennant Race: Konami's MSX2 baseball, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1988 MSX2 baseball, 100% explained and commented to 43.7%. The six teams with their cards, the rules as the code has them (the ten-run rule, pitch speeds of 80 to 199 km/h, the TEAM EDIT caps), the PENNANT league and how it saves to disk or to the Game Master 2's SRAM. 26 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine and 6 pictures drawn from the ROM, checked against openMSX.

entry.title: Konami's Game Master 2: the cheat cartridge, its SRAM, Tennis and Hockey and a biorhythm, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1987 cheat cartridge, 100% explained and commented to 40.1%. How it gets into 30 games, MSX2 ones too, through H.TIMI; its 68 signatures; the SRAM file system; the two-player Tennis and Hockey with its rules and nine tunes; and the biorhythm. 24 screens drawn from the ROM on MSX and MSX2, checked against the running cartridge and openMSX.

entry.title: Konami's Game Master: the counts redone with 67 cartridges
entry.summary: The collection has grown since the Game Master was published, and two of its claims no longer held. The hook it looks for in the game's start-up is in 53 of the 60 Konami cartridges: the seven without it are the six MSX2 ones and the European version of the Game Master itself. The second header is in 16 games, not eight, and the rule by year still holds for all of them.

entry.title: Ganbare Goemon: the province map and the lord's hall, animated
entry.summary: What theNestruo asked for in issue #5: the map shown before each area, with the province name in kanji, and the whole end-of-stage scene, with the retainers coming in, bowing and the lord speaking, one per stage, plus the angry lord. The scene is the cartridge's own code run frame by frame, drawn by ours, and both are checked against openMSX.
